messages.subject: ./configure does not create Makefile in OS X (Lion)

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
  I want to use the RPostgreSQL package on Mac OS X 10.7.2. I have 
installed R 2.14.1 and DBI 0.4.3. Is a binary for Mac OS still not 
available, as the following page shows?

  http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RPostgreSQL/index.html

  I tried to install from the source, but after the usual call to 
./configure, I got the following output, but no Makefile got created. 
However, ./configure does not report any error, either. Could you please 
explain what I should do as the next step?

messages.body_plain:
On 6 January 2012 at 14:15, Bibudh Lahiri wrote:
|  
|   Hi,
|   I want to use the RPostgreSQL package on Mac OS X 10.7.2. I have installed R
| 2.14.1 and DBI 0.4.3. Is a binary for Mac OS still not available, as the
| following page shows?
| 
|   http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RPostgreSQL/index.html
| 
|   I tried to install from the source, but after the usual call to ./configure,
| I got the following output, but no Makefile got created. However, ./configure

You do not need one; R creates those implicitly and actually _recommends not
having one_.

You install an R package by saying

    $ R CMD INSTALL foo_1.2-3.tar.gz

so just run 'R CMD INSTALL' over the RPostgreSQL tarball, or alternatively,
the top-level directory.

| does not report any error, either. Could you please explain what I should do as
| the next step?
| 
| checking for gcc... gcc
| checking for C compiler default output file name... a.out
| checking whether the C compiler works... yes
| checking whether we are cross compiling... no
| checking for suffix of executables...
| checking for suffix of object files... o
| checking whether we are using the GNU C compiler... yes
| checking whether gcc accepts -g... yes
| checking for gcc option to accept ISO C89... none needed
| checking build system type... x86_64-apple-darwin11.2.0
| checking host system type... x86_64-apple-darwin11.2.0
| checking target system type... x86_64-apple-darwin11.2.0
| checking for pg_config... /usr/local/bin/pg_config
| checking for "/usr/local/Cellar/postgresql/
| 9.0.4/include/libpq-fe.h"... yes

That's key, so you have Pg sources.

Everything should "just work".

Dirk

| config.status: creating src/Makevar

|    Thanks
|                 Bibudh

messages.body_plain:
My earlier experience with R was based on Windows. 
  I was getting the following error when I was trying to load the 
RPostgreSQL library in R,

  Error: package ‘RPostgreSQL’ is not installed for 'arch=i386'

  however, doing the following solved the problem

  R --arch=i386 CMD INSTALL RPostgreSQL_0.3-1.tar 
--configure-args='--with-pgsql-libraries=<My Postgres lib> 
--with-pgsql-includes=<My postgres include>'

  Thanks for your help.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,

As of today, OS X binary become available in cran main repository.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RPostgreSQL/

It may take a few more days to circulate on mirrors, though.

The only remaining error target is the windows development version (r-devel).
http://cran.r-project.org/web/checks/check_results_RPostgreSQL.html
